title: mimid-server storage for packaging: robust single replica, Postgres on demand
description:
Decided with Mark 2026-11-20.

Agent side: keep SQLite. agent.sqlite (mimid-1vul.10) holds MLS secrets, the delivery journal and the chat records in one database, so decrypt-and-store is atomic. Not in scope here.

Server side, in order:
1. At packaging: a robust single replica. Continuous backup (Litestream or similar) of the sqlx SQLite database, fast restart, documented restore and failover. Do this first.
2. When a shop asks for Postgres: a storage abstraction in crates/mimid-server/src/store/ with SQLite the default and Postgres an option, still one active replica. Facts as of 2026-11-20: sqlx 0.9 SqlitePool, 123 sqlx::query calls, 10 migrations (STRICT tables, BLOB columns), about 13 SQLite-specific constructs (pragmas, ON CONFLICT, RETURNING). Postgres needs its own migrations, $1 placeholders and BYTEA. The hub keeps no OpenMLS storage: each room's Observer is an in-memory PublicGroup rebuilt from the room table's GroupInfo and ratchet tree, so no OpenMLS Postgres provider is needed.
3. Several replicas, only on real demand: shard rooms across replicas (each room owned by one replica, which keeps the per-room Commit order single-writer) rather than row locks, plus a shared change bus for EventSource fanout (Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY or a broker).
